newsitem.title: POLAND: Demand seen small at Polish fixed bond tender.
newsitem.headline: Demand seen small at Polish fixed bond tender.

text.p: Poland's fixed bond tender on Wednesday may attract very few investors as the finance ministry is unlikely to raise its yields to match those on the secondary market after the central bank rate rise, dealers said.

"The demand will be miserable. No one expects the finance ministry to accept the potential bids... as bonds trade at very high yields on the secondary market," said Krzysztof Kozuchowski, debt dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.

On Monday the National Bank of Poland raised its two main rates by two and 2.5 points to 27 and 24.5 percent for the lombard and discount rates, respectively, to curb credit activity, cool domestic demand and stop the widening of the country's current account gap.
Dealers said the tender was likely to resemble the previous two auctions, when the ministry sold only fractions of the offer because it would not lower the price in line with market expectations.
The treasury is offering a total of one billion zlotys worth of 12-percent five-year bonds maturing October 12, 2002 and 15-percent two-year bonds maturing October 12, 1999.
Dealers expected the ministry might sell 50 million zlotys worth of five-year paper and 100-150 million of the shorter bond.
"The ministry may set the ceiling at yields of 22.30-40 percent for the two-year bonds, which will hardly be acceptable for the market," said Marcin Rzechowski, dealer at Societe Generale in Warsaw.
On the secondary market two-year paper traded at 23.50 to 23.80 percent. There were no deals in five-year bonds, which the market views as an illiquid instrument.
